subject: zoology
question_text: What is Gause's principle? When is it applicable?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.62, VSAQ 171). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The principle
lines: two closely related species competing for
The weaker competitor is eliminated in due
steps.why: The principle has a result as well as a statement, so the second line is needed: it names what happens to the loser, which is the part that makes the principle useful.
common_mistakes: Writing that the two species cannot live in the same place at all. They cannot co-exist INDEFINITELY.
Leaving out the outcome. The weaker competitor is eliminated.
steps.memory_tip: Same resource, same place, long enough time — one of the two species goes.
steps.margin_note: The statement in one sentence, then one line on what happens to the weaker species.

steps.label: When it applies

lines.text: It holds only when resources are limited

steps.why: The second half of the question is a condition, and it is the part most often left out; without a shortage there is no competition, so the principle simply does not apply.
common_mistakes: Writing that the principle always applies. It applies only when resources are LIMITED.
Answering only the first half of the question. The condition is a separate mark.
steps.memory_tip: No shortage, no competition. The principle needs the resources to run short.
steps.margin_note: One line for the condition and one for why. Both halves of the question must be answered.

insider_note: The question has two halves and the second one, the condition, carries a full mark — never stop after the statement.
